---
title: "User guide"
---

A model is a specification. Solving does not change it.

```python
import geap

model = geap.PowerUtilityModel()
res = model.solve()
print(res.summary())
res.compare("equity", "bill").premium
```

## Specify

Keyword overrides merge onto Mehra and Prescott (1985).

```{python}
import geap

print(geap.PowerUtilityModel(gamma=2))
print(geap.PowerUtilityModel(delta=0.96, gamma=10))
```

Extra claims are levered consumption. `equity` is the Lucas tree
($\phi = 1$). `bill` has no leverage.

```{python}
print(geap.PowerUtilityModel(claims={"high": {"phi": 3}}))
```

## Solve

The state space is two points. `method="grid"` and
`method="analytical"` are the same numbers.

```{python}
res = geap.PowerUtilityModel().solve()
print(res.expected_returns)
```

A counterfactual is a new model:

```{python}
base = geap.PowerUtilityModel()
print(base.replace(gamma=2).solve().compare("equity", "bill").premium)
print(base.gamma)
```

## Simulate

`simulate` draws finite annual samples from the chain and averages the
sample means, the same object as Table VII in the long-run-risks
family.

```{python}
sim = geap.PowerUtilityModel().simulate(n_samples=200, years=100, seed=0)
print(sim.compare("equity", "bill").premium)
```

Source: Mehra and Prescott (1985).
